text.title: Dual-Write Shadow-Read Template — Procedure
text.summary: Nine steps in the order the migration runs: declare entity types and their gates, implement the version-guarded dual write outside the old transaction, declare and schedule reconciliation, enable dual-write and backfill in that order with verification, define the four flags and the reverse order, turn on sampled shadow reads with a bounded candidate, evaluate the numeric gate and flip reads with a named approver, hold the retention window and rehearse the flip-back, then validate and file. Each step names its rule and the skeleton section it fills.

step.name: declare-entity-types-and-gates
step.input: The tables or aggregates being migrated; their primary keys and a monotonic version per row (row version, `updated_at`, or log sequence number); the fields that legitimately differ between stores.
step.action: For each entity type record `primary_key`, `version_field`, `parity_excluded_fields` (auto-generated timestamps, surrogate ids, search vectors) and the gate: `mismatch_ratio_max`, `window_hours`, `min_comparisons`. Write these before any shadow read runs and set `cutover.gate_declared_before_shadow` true. Fill `# Entity types and gates` in `templates/skeleton.md.j2`.
step.decision-gate: A gate written after seeing the parity number is a gate that can be lowered under schedule pressure (r-cutover-gate-numeric, r-shadow-read-parity-diff).

step.name: implement-version-guarded-dual-write
step.input: The write path of the old store; the new store's upsert semantics.
step.action: Fan out every write to the new store as an upsert keyed by primary key with a compare-and-set on the version field, outside the old store's transaction. Route failures to a durable `retry_queue`, emit `dual_write_failures_total`, and set an `alert_threshold`. Record `dual_write`. Fill `# Dual write`.
step.decision-gate: A plain insert or unversioned overwrite is fm-non-idempotent-fanout; a new-store write inside the request path is fm-new-store-fails-request (r-dual-write-idempotent-writes, r-old-store-authoritative).

step.name: declare-and-schedule-reconciliation
step.input: The key space of the old store; the scheduler.
step.action: Name the key-walk job that compares each old-store record to the new store and repairs the new store, set its `cadence` (at least weekly, hourly for high-write entities) and `max_repairs_per_run`, and emit `reconciliation_repairs_total`. Record `reconciliation` with `declared_before_dual_write` true. Fill `# Reconciliation`.
step.decision-gate: Trusting dual-write to be complete is fm-no-reconciliation; two stores are never atomic (r-reconciliation-job-required).

step.name: enable-dual-write-then-backfill
step.input: The `dual_write_on` flag; the historical data partitioned for backfill.
step.action: Flip `flags.dual_write_on`, then start the backfill using the same version-guarded upsert. Verify per-partition row counts and a content checksum against the old store and record `backfill` with every verification true. Do not report any parity number until this is done. Fill `# Backfill`.
step.decision-gate: Backfill before dual-write leaves a gap; backfill with plain overwrites clobbers live updates (r-backfill-before-shadow, fm-backfill-clobbers-live).

step.name: define-flags-and-reverse-order
step.action: Create four runtime flags — `dual_write_on`, `shadow_read_on`, `read_from_new_on`, `write_to_old_off` — flippable without a deploy, write the reverse order (write_to_old_off, read_from_new_on, shadow_read_on, dual_write_on), and set `retention_window_days` for old-store writes after read cutover. Record `flags`. Fill `# Flags and rollback`.
step.decision-gate: A single combined migrated flag has no rollback once the old store stops receiving writes (r-rollback-flag-per-stage, fm-old-store-dropped-early).

step.name: enable-sampled-shadow-reads
step.input: The read path; the measured old-store p99; the `sampling_flag`.
step.action: Issue every sampled read to both stores, compare with a normalising comparator honouring `parity_excluded_fields`, return the old store's result, bound the new-store read by `candidate_timeout_ms` at or under `old_store_p99_ms`, swallow and count its exceptions, publish `shadow_read_mismatch_ratio` per entity type and retain mismatching keys. Start `sampling_percent_initial` low. Record `shadow_read`. Fill `# Shadow read`.
step.decision-gate: A raw-row comparator is fm-parity-noise; 100 percent sampling with no timeout is fm-shadow-read-latency (r-shadow-read-parity-diff, r-shadow-read-no-user-impact).

step.name: evaluate-gate-and-flip-reads
step.input: The parity dashboard over the declared window; the named approver.
step.action: When every entity type's `shadow_read_mismatch_ratio` is under its `mismatch_ratio_max` over `window_hours` with at least `min_comparisons`, link the evaluation as `cutover.gate_evaluation_url`, have `read_from_new_approver` review it, flip `read_from_new_on`, and set `read_from_new_flipped` true. Keep `write_to_old_off` false.
step.output: `cutover` with evaluation URL and approver; reads on the new store.
step.decision-gate: "Parity looks fine" is not the gate; a quiet entity with twelve reads does not pass on luck (r-cutover-gate-numeric; human checkpoint).

step.name: hold-retention-and-rehearse-flipback
step.action: Keep old-store writes on for the retention window. Once, flip `read_from_new_on` back to the old store, confirm callers see correct data, flip forward again, and record the rehearsal URL in `evidence[]` with `read_flipback_rehearsed_before_write_off` true. Only then may `write_to_old_off_approver` approve turning off writes to the old store, the last flag in the documented order.
step.decision-gate: Write-to-old off before the window and the rehearsal is fm-old-store-dropped-early (r-rollback-flag-per-stage).

step.name: validate-and-file
step.input: The filled skeleton and its JSON form.
step.action: Run `scripts/validate-dual-write-shadow-read-template.py --file <runbook.json>`; fix every violation; commit the runbook to `.product/dual-write-shadow-read-template/` with the reconciliation dashboard, backfill verification, gate evaluation and rehearsal in `evidence[]`.
step.output: A runbook that validates and records each production-affecting flip with its approver.

list.item: Reads were flipped only after the declared numeric gate held for every entity type, with the evaluation linked and a named approver.
Old-store writes continued through the retention window and the flip-back was rehearsed before write-to-old went off.
Reconciliation repairs and dual-write failures are both metrics with declared budgets, not assumptions.
